questions.known_context: Al_0.75 and Al_1.5 both contain Al/Ni enriched B2 phases. Al_1.5 shows a high density of spherical precipitates in the A2 matrix. Both multiphase samples show precipitation, unlike the single-phase sample.
questions.unresolved_information: Specific comparative metrics (size, density, composition) of precipitates forming *within* the B2 phase of Al_0.75 versus Al_1.5, or if the B2 phase in Al_0.75 is more stable than in Al_1.5.
evidence_spans: The precipitates in the A2 phases of Al 1.5 CoCrFeNi have the largest size and the average precipitate sizes in the Cr, Fe-enriched fcc and A2 phases are obviously larger than those in the Al, Ni-enriched B2 phases for both HEAs

research_thread.scientific_problem: Determining the mechanism of radiation-induced precipitation stability in multiphase High Entropy Alloys (HEAs) compared to single-phase systems.
research_thread.sample_lineage: Al_0.75 CoCrFeNi (fcc + B2), Al_0.1 CoCrFeNi (single fcc), Al_1.5 CoCrFeNi (B2 + A2)
research_thread.baseline: As-prepared microstructures characterized by XRD, SEM, TEM
research_thread.conditions: Ion irradiation with Au ions, varying fluences
research_thread.structure: As-prepared: Al_0.75 is fcc+B2. Irradiated: Multiphase samples develop precipitates, single-phase remains stable.
research_thread.outcome: Single-phase (Al_0.1) shows high stability; Multiphase (Al_0.75, Al_1.5) show significant precipitation and phase enrichment.
research_thread.mechanism: High configurational entropy in single-phase reduces thermodynamic driving force and kinetic mobility; Multiphase stability limited by lower entropy and phase separation driving force.
research_thread.hypothesis_value: High configurational entropy is the primary factor for irradiation tolerance, but phase stability in multiphase systems is also governed by local composition and defect kinetics.
alternative_explanations: Precipitation in multiphase is due to local compositional fluctuations rather than global entropy effects.
Defect recombination rates differ due to the presence of phase boundaries.
boundaries: Single-phase stability limited to Al_0.1; Precipitation occurs for Al > 0.1
TEM detectability limit for precipitate size in stable samples.
null_or_negative_results: No precipitates observed in Al_0.1 CoCrFeNi even at highest fluence.
missing_information: Quantitative comparison of precipitate evolution in the B2 phase between x=0.75 and x=1.5
Atomic diffusion coefficients for specific phases under irradiation.

questions.why_it_matters: Distinguishing between processing-induced precipitation and irradiation-induced precipitation is crucial for defining the baseline stability of the material before testing irradiation effects.
questions.known_context: Al_1.5 is as-fabricated with a B2+A2 structure. TEM shows ~80 nm spherical precipitates in the as-fabricated state. Irradiation causes precipitation in multiphase samples.

research_thread.scientific_problem: Differentiating between processing-induced microstructural features and radiation-induced changes in high-Al content multiphase HEAs.
research_thread.baseline: As-fabricated state with pre-existing ~80 nm precipitates and strong elemental segregation.
research_thread.structure: B2+A2 duplex with spherical precipitates. Strong segregation: B2 (Al,Co,Ni), A2 (Fe,Cr).
research_thread.outcome: Multiphase nature leads to precipitation; baseline microstructure already contains precipitates.
research_thread.mechanism: Segregation driven by mixing enthalpy and low entropy. Radiation may enhance defect clustering on existing interfaces or in segregated regions.
research_thread.hypothesis_value: Pre-existing precipitation in high-Al multiphase HEAs suggests a lower threshold for radiation damage accumulation compared to single-phase alloys, driven by thermodynamic instability rather than just kinetic factors.
alternative_explanations: Precipitates in as-fabricated state are metastable and dissolve before irradiation effects dominate.
Radiation induces amorphization rather than precipitation in highly segregated phases.
boundaries: High Al content (1.5) leads to multiphase structure and pre-existing precipitates.
Segregation levels exceed 84 at.% in specific phases.
null_or_negative_results: None explicitly, but the contrast with the single-phase sample highlights the instability of the multiphase baseline.
missing_information: Post-irradiation microstructure evolution of the specific ~80 nm precipitates in Al_1.5.
Defect accumulation rates in segregated B2 vs A2 phases.

evidence_spans: The sample densities for x = 0.1, 0.75 and 1.5, which were measured by Archimedes method, are 8.1, 7.4 and 6.9 g·cm −3 , respectively.
The microstructures of as-prepared Al x CoCrFeNi HEAs ( x = 0.1, 0.75 and 1.5) are single fcc, fcc plus ordered bcc (B2) and B2 plus disordered bcc (A2), respectively.

For x = 1.5, TEM microstructural characterization of the as-fabricated alloy ( Fig. 1(c) ) revealed a high density of spherical precipitates with average diameter of ~80 nm distributed throughout the matrix.

For example, Al 1.5 CoCrFeNi exhibits of a B2 and A2 duplex microstructure with the total concentration of Al, Co and Ni in B2 phases and Fe, Cr in A2 phases reaching 85.5 at. % and 84.7 at. %, respectively.
